what: GameStop sells video games, consoles and collectibles through about 3,000 stores, and since 2024 it has put much of its cash into bitcoin and treasury holdings.
customers: Gamers buying and trading in games and hardware, and collectors buying trading cards and figures.
moat: A trade-in business other retailers do not run: buying used games and consoles and reselling them earns a much higher margin than selling new ones, and the stores are where that happens.
risks: Games are increasingly downloaded rather than bought on disc, which removes the core business
Revenue fell from $6.0B to $3.6B in four years and stores keep closing
The share price has long been driven by retail investor enthusiasm rather than results, and only one analyst covers it
opportunities: $9.0B of cash, well above the $13.6B market value once the convertible debt is counted
Profitable again at $893M of net income, with $688M of free cash flow
Collectibles and trading cards grow while game discs shrink, and carry better margins
watch: Comparable store sales and what the company does with its cash pile.
